student_question.stem: A reliable low-voltage battery, working bulb and intact bare copper wires form a closed loop. Copper is an ideal conductor. A small dry plastic block is placed under the middle of one wire. The block touches the outside of the bare wire but does not cut it, separate any connection or touch any other circuit part. The bulb remains lit. Plastic is an ideal insulator. A pupil claims, “The bulb should go out whenever plastic touches a wire.”
student_question.diagram_alt: All information is supplied in the text and data table. No external diagram is required.
student_question.question: Which statement correctly evaluates the claim?

options.text: The claim is correct because plastic changes copper into an insulator.
The claim is correct because current must enter every object touching a wire.
The claim is incorrect because plastic becomes a conductor beside a battery.
The claim is incorrect because the copper path is still unbroken.

answer.explanation_en: The plastic does not interrupt the copper wire. The conducting loop remains complete, so the bulb stays lit.
answer.scoring: 2 marks for the correct option; 0 otherwise. Practice scoring, subject to reviewer approval.

distractor_rationales.issue: Touching plastic does not change copper's conducting property.
The loop can carry current through the copper without current passing through the plastic support.
The plastic remains an insulator. Its position beside the circuit does not change its property.

syllabus_mapping.item_evidence: Recognises that an external support does not break an intact conducting loop.

syllabus_mapping.item_evidence: Rejects the misconception that contact with an insulator stops conduction through an intact wire.
